propositions: BindingStore is a 799-line module with tangled concerns: byte persistence, lifecycle policy, retirement, recovery, and GET rotation, with no cohesive ownership of new safety rules and production code mutating inner entries via shallow all_bindings() query.

A mechanical split of BindingStore must preserve existing imports, method signatures, unknown-field handling, and exact JSON serialization (indent=2, sorted keys, trailing newline) without regressing crash safety, index lag, identity, or selective-publication behavior.

Retirement completion must follow a durable-tombstone rule: a live forward/reverse pair is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities agree, and only explicit unretire revokes retirement intent; automatic liveness signals never resurrect a tombstoned identity.
Live recovery must run after configuration snapshot and exclusive lock validation but before remote issue fetch or binding walk, to prevent interleaving new liveness evidence with completion.

The three extracted internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, incomplete-operation recovery) must sit behind a single unchanged public BindingStore facade while enabling narrow mutation seams to replace direct mutation-through-query patterns.

Four documented behaviors were never implemented (ambiguous-double-bind abort, lifecycle alert deduping, comment-key immutability, rich-emission save-gating) and required corrections to docstrings or filed defects rather than behavior changes within the extraction scope.
